one: ML systems: efficiency across the data, training, and inference stack, with hardware-software co-design.
pos: CS 229S looks at machine learning from a systems perspective: models are bigger, data is larger, hardware is more heterogeneous — where is the performance bottleneck? It covers data pipelines, distributed training, GPUs/accelerators, networking, inference serving, and compilation, for people who want to work on MLSys/infrastructure.
topics: **Distributed training**: data, model, and pipeline parallelism
**Inference serving**: batching, scheduling, KV cache, latency
**Cases and project**: performance analysis of real systems
prereq: CS 224N or CS 229; systems/architecture background helps.
assess: Assignments plus a project, focused on systems implementation and performance analysis. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: People who want to work on MLSys, inference infrastructure, or training platforms; systems people moving into ML.
tips: Pair with CS 149 (parallel computing) and CS 217 (accelerators). Understand the roofline model and communication costs first.
note: Not offered in the 2026–27 ExploreCourses listing; no stable course-site link found.
